You have attempted this same task before and did not succeed. These are the plans you wrote after those attempts.
Trial #1: New plan: I failed because I stopped the exploration prematurely after visiting only four rooms, leaving unvisited rooms (like the one accessible from the Exercise room via east) undiscovered. Additionally, my graph construction was incomplete; I failed to record the edges I traversed (e.g., the connection between Media room and Playroom, or Garage and Exercise room) in the `edges` dictionary, only updating the `nodes` list. Next time, I will maintain a persistent mental map of all visited nodes and edges, ensuring every transition is added to the `edges` object before moving. I will only output "DONE" when I have explicitly confirmed that all currently available directions from every visited node have been explored and no new rooms remain reachable.

New plan: I failed because I entered a repetitive loop between the Media room and Playroom, repeatedly moving south and north without ever exploring the new direction (east) available in the Garage. My strategy lacked a mechanism to track which directions from each visited node had already been attempted, causing me to ignore unexplored paths. Next time, I will maintain a strict record of visited nodes and the specific directions taken from each. Before moving, I will explicitly check if any available direction from the current room has not yet been tried; if so, I will prioritize that new direction. I will only output "DONE" when I have confirmed that all reachable nodes have been visited and all available directions from every node in the graph have been exhausted.
